title: Ground-Based Thermal Infrared Imaging of Hyperthermal Springs in a Built Heritage Environment: Radiometric Challenges and Thermal Anomaly Mapping at As Burgas (Ourense, Spain)
content: Urban hyperthermal springs embedded in historic ensembles are a demanding setting for thermal remote sensing: extreme temperature contrasts, materials of different emissivity within a few metres and vapour along the optical path. This study applies ground-based radiometric infrared thermography to the two monumental fountains of As Burgas (Ourense, Spain), a site protected as a Property of Cultural Interest. The raw sensor values of 67 thermograms acquired with a low-cost smartphone-attached camera were processed with a custom radiometric model, RGB–TIR co-registration, regions of interest, line profiles, anomaly classification and sensitivity analysis. The water reached radiometric temperatures of 61.9 °C at Burga de Arriba and 68.5 °C at Burga de Abaixo (67.4 °C with water emissivity and field conditions, within 0.4–1.1 °C of published spring temperatures). The adjacent masonry was heated by up to 6.8 °C, and anomalies without visible water, such as the drainage network, were detected. Radiometric parameterisation introduced little uncertainty (≤2.5 °C), compared with an underestimation of 6–19 °C caused by spatial resolution in overview images. A replicable protocol for monitoring built hydrothermal heritage is proposed.
